item.content:encoded:
Hello. I'm PoeticStanza. I'm kinda a lurker on the site, but I do occasionally like to make minor edits for grammar and syntaxes. I may end up contributing a bit to certain experiment logs, namely some of the more creative experiments like 914, 261, and 1459. I don't currently have any large ambitions to write articles but I do look forward to enjoying all the site has to offer.

Why I joined: I mostly want the chance to read articles unimpeded and maybe add to some of the more community-driven experiments.

What I want to do: mostly lurk and vote, but participate in interesting projects

Hobbies/Interests: I've been a creative writer for a while, and I'm very passionate about music.

What keeps me up at night: bees and clowns (particularly Bobble). There's also my everyday existential crises and the idea that nothing I do in life will ever matter in the long run.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, fellow members. I am a freelance horror writer currently going to school at Full Sail U for creative writing. I was always a fan of the SCP genre of things, since long before I started writing. You could say, among other things, it somewhat inspired me to my own writing. And now that I am confident enough in my particular form of horror, I have decided to present myself among you all and begin the process of adding my own work to this glorious work of art we know as the SCP Foundation.

Personally, I have a deep and longing fascination with the horrors of the mind. This sprouted from an experiment I performed on myself with lucidity and the effects of uncontrolled experimentation. You see, the lucid state in which I brought upon myself didn't exactly stop when I wanted it to. It became abundantly clear to me that no matter what I did, I would eventually be conscious when I went to sleep. In this time spent in a lucid state, I began to feel as if I was being followed by something I had not created there. Or perhaps someone I had created unknowingly. Eventually, the method I had used to gain lucidity wore and with it, the state.

Nevertheless, I lay awake at night knowing that he… or it… is still in there somewhere.

Sorry if that was a little too much.

item.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers: Re: Damian Thorne's Needlessly [REDACTED] Intro
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Damian Thorne! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

Well, keep your secrets to yourself then - regardless though, welcome to the site. I'd really want to say something more, but without your input, I can't really do much here. I'll say this much - I very much hope you enjoy your time here on-site and achieve all of the goals you're aiming for.

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!
